messages:
maria: heads up — I prototyped an "early-exit" sampler for high-volume routes to reduce OTLP exporter load. It drops low-value spans earlier in the pipeline instead of after export.

devon: curious, what's the heuristic? head-only?

maria: hybrid. idea is: fast prefix/head sampling for bulk routes (0.5-2% rate), plus deterministic tagging so we can retroactively fetch tails if needed. then a separate tail rule picks up slow/err spans with keep=1.0.

sriram: deterministic tagging = hash(trace_id + route) so we can reconstruct? risk of state explosion for very bursty routes.

maria: yeah deterministic per-tenant-route with a windowed salt. e.g., hash(trace_id + route + window_id) to limit retention keys. window_id = floor(now / 300) for 5m windows.

anya: can you paste the config snippet? want to see how it looks in console rollout.

maria: sure:
```yaml
telemetry: 
  sampling: 
    mode: early_exit_hybrid
    head: 
      rate: 0.01 # 1% head for high-volume routes
      deterministic_window_seconds: 300
    tail_rules:
      - latency_ms: 200
        keep: 1.0
      - http_status: [500,502,503]
        keep: 1.0
```

devon: nice. how do we measure cost improvement? need token/span saved estimates.

maria: rough numbers from locally replayed traffic: exporter bytes down ~68%, ingestion cost (per-tenant) down ~55% for top-10 routes.

sriram: what about cold-start for debugging? if head samples drop the initial spans for a trace we might lose context.

maria: good point. we keep the first N spans for sampled traces (N=3) and also keep any span that has an error tag. early-exit only drops low-priority informational spans after that.

anya: UX question — in the console rollout, can we show "visibility score" per route so PMs see how many traces are still reconstructible?

devon: we should expose a small estimator: sampled_traces / estimated_total_traces and tail-capture-coverage metric. console can show a 7d trend and a cost delta preview for toggling rate.

sriram: edge-case: very low-volume tenants — deterministic hashing + 5m windows could accidentally keep too many windows with single traces. Need min-ttl compaction.

maria: agreed. plan: if tenant route < 1 req/min on avg, fallback to aggressive tail-only capture (keep everything for errors, head rate -> 0). avoids creating lots of windows.

anya: rollout plan? feature flag + canary on a few non-critical services?

maria: yes. feature-flagged config in console per-customer. step 1: enable on internal staging routes for 24h, step 2: 2% of production traffic across non-SRE tenants, monitor visibility and error-investigation latency, step 3: 25% routes.

devon: let's add a schema migration for exporter metrics so the backend can compute pre/post cost delta without replay. something like: exporter._sampling_decision = {"reason":"head|tail|rule-XYZ"}.

sriram: +1. add audit log entries for deterministic_window changes. customers will ask why their debug traces disappeared.

anya: also add a small "fetch missed trace" API that lets support query storage by deterministic window + trace hash and try reconstructing if we stored some span fragments. Docs will show best-effort only.

maria: ops-bot: can you queue a canary deploy for the telemetry pipeline with the earliest-exit sampler enabled for staging?

ops-bot: Deploy requested by maria. Canary rollout queued to staging cluster at 2025-06-15T03:12:00Z.

devon: I'll add the console toggle + preview panel. We'll want an AB test to measure mean time to investigate (MTTI) for incidents before/after.

sriram: last thing — make sure exporters with backpressure gracefully drop low-priority spans instead of blocking. early-exit helps but exporter backpressure path needs a non-blocking queue fallback.

maria: noted. I'll open a follow-up PR for exporter queue ABI changes. Thanks everyone, will post the initial canary report in this thread. :rocket:
